rationale: Fake weather or traffic data can disrupt routing and cause mid-air conflict risks.
Leaking strategic plans compromises operational confidentiality rather than immediate flight safety.
Compromising the SSOT poisons dependent U-Space services simultaneously across the board.
Manipulating local sensors or IMUs can cause immediate physical crashes of individual UAS.
False telemetry injection into tracking systems creates phantom traffic and masks conflicts.
Tampering with audit trails hinders post-incident accountability without immediate safety impact.
Exploiting regulatory loopholes undermines compliance oversight and legal frameworks over time.
False identities allow illegal flight authorization but lack direct operational safety feedback loops.
Bypassing signature verification grants unauthorized flights, creating severe collision risks.
Removing no-fly zones allows drones to inadvertently enter dangerous or restricted airspace.
GNSS spoofing and jamming disrupt positioning globally, risking widespread deviation and crashes.
Physical sabotage at vertiports compromises landing zones and ground operations locally.
Injecting fake geofences causes drones to fly into unauthorized or restricted zones.
Hardware backdoors or compromised firmware directly jeopardize individual flight control and safety.
Compromising regulatory oversight systems impairs accountability and compliance enforcement.
Compromised components or supply chains introduce widespread backdoors across deployed fleets.
Power outages or BMS manipulation shut down ground stations or cause mid-air battery failures.
Flooding the API gateway disrupts all U-Space services and halts flight authorizations volume-wide.
SQL injection leads to mass data exfiltration and corruption of operational flight records.
Jamming or intercepting C2 links can trigger fail-safe crashes or loss of drone control.
API key leakage enables bulk exfiltration of sensitive flight plan data without direct safety impact.
